readiness_rule.borderline: If scores are rising but below target, use the next official exam and focused repair to judge readiness. Protect the 10-day scheduling deadline.
readiness_rule.reconsider_date: If full lengths remain well below target, sections remain unfinished, or a section stays below 126, consider a later date before the scheduling deadline.

workload_policy.budget_role: planned_hours is the weekly capacity budget, not a promise that every upper-bound estimate fits.
workload_policy.validation: Fail if the low estimate exceeds the budget. Show midpoint and upper-bound risks; never clamp estimates to fit.
workload_policy.execution: Protect full-lengths, answer review, and sleep. If the time cap is reached, move unfinished reading into the next content block by replacing new volume; never stack it on top.
workload_policy.maintenance: Chapter days include a 10-minute spaced-retrieval loop plus selective Anki/mistake-log work, all within the existing 15-30 minute maintenance allowance. Operational mode blocks already include maintenance; exam/review days have no extra quota.
workload_policy.estimates: Mode ranges and question review allowances are planning assumptions, not measured completion times. The midpoint is a sensitivity check, not a statistical forecast.

retention_protocol.daily_retrieval: Use the first 10 minutes of each chapter day for closed-book recall: one prompt from the previous study day, one from about seven days earlier, and one high-yield relationship, pathway, or equation. Check notes only after the attempt.
retention_protocol.question_mix: Mix current-topic and earlier-topic science questions as recall improves; review every answer before adding volume.
retention_protocol.feedback: For every wrong, flagged, or guessed-correct item, state why the chosen answer failed, write one concise correction, and reattempt the idea closed book in 7-14 days before rereading the explanation.
retention_protocol.cards: Create or unsuspend Anki cards only for retrieval failures, repeated misses, or high-yield facts. Keep cards and mistake-log work inside the existing maintenance window.
retention_protocol.weekly: At the end of Monday's work, convert at most three recurring weaknesses into retrieval prompts for the next week.
retention_protocol.cars: Start with three reviewed passages per week, then build to four or five. Work toward ten minutes per passage while reviewing the main point, stance, evidence, and every miss.
retention_protocol.minimum_viable_day: If time is short, complete the 10-minute retrieval loop plus the smallest scheduled practice unit and leave the remaining steps incomplete. Do not mark the full day complete.

blocks.text: MCAT Study Plan: September 22, 2026 to March 19, 2027
March 19 planning date | Score goal: 520 | 26 study weeks

Begin with three chapters and three reviewed CARS passages per week. Build toward content-heavy weeks of up to six chapters while keeping question review, one rest day, and full-length review protected.

items: Five chapters are documented as covered: Physics and Math 10-11 and General Chemistry 1-3. Record the additional completed chapter in the tracker when identified.
The first three weeks establish a steady routine and include an unscored diagnostic on October 10.
Finish the remaining first-pass chapters by late January. Use CARS strategy chapters selectively when passage review reveals a specific weakness.
Keep six official scored full lengths spaced from December through March, with Friday protected for rest and Sunday and Monday protected for review.
March 19 is a planning date until a seat is booked. Enter the confirmed date in Exams.
Review every answer before counting a practice set complete. Wrong, flagged, and guessed-correct questions get one concrete fix and a retest in 7-14 days.
Start chapter days with 10 minutes of closed-book retrieval. Use a full read for weak foundations, objectives and checks for rusty topics, and questions first for familiar material.
One CARS passage means one passage plus review of the main point, author stance, evidence, and every miss.
If a week runs long, reduce new reading or question volume before cutting answer review, sleep, or the protected rest day.
On a short day, complete the smallest scheduled practice unit and retrieval loop. Leave other steps open rather than marking the whole day complete.
